positions.name: S2 (Prose Edda)
positions.description: Son of Odin and the giantess Járnsaxa (or the earth Jörd)

how_we_present_it: We note the variant; the core is that Thor is the son of Odin.

positions.name: S2
positions.description: Son of Odin and Angrboða (odd, since she is elsewhere Loki's wife)

how_we_present_it: Both variants stored; the sources are not consistent.

positions.name: S2
positions.description: Two separate divine tribes who later merge

positions.name: Interpretive
positions.description: Some scholars see the 'two tribes' as a later literary construction

how_we_present_it: We present the 'two tribes' as the sources present it, and note the scholarly interpretation separately.

positions.name: Archaeological
positions.description: The gods are worshipped from at least the 5th–8th c. CE (place-names, runestones)

positions.name: Literary
positions.description: The main sources (Eddas) are 13th c. CE

how_we_present_it: We make clear that the 13th-c. texts preserve older oral traditions; the worship is much older than the texts.

positions.name: S2
positions.description: 'Blood-related' to the gods but not a true Æsir; a giant/trickster

positions.name: Interpretive
positions.description: Some scholars see Loki as a 'chthonic' or 'liminal' figure

how_we_present_it: We present Loki as the sources do (not a true Æsir) and note the interpretation.
